title: FORGIVE OR FORGET: UNDERSTANDING THE CONTEXT OF HATE IN AUDIO RETRIEVAL SYSTEMS

bias_targets.methodology: The paper evaluates the retrieval of audio containing hate speech by transcribing clips via automatic speech recognition (ASR) and classifying the resulting text with a toxicity detection model. It also identifies hate-driven retrieval biases by comparing model outputs against counterfactual prompts injected with toxic intent.

Measuring the prevalence of various toxic categories (profanities, pornographic language, slurs, violence, and bullying) in retrieved audio. The paper uses 'Success Rate', 'Accuracy', and 'Sensitivity' metrics to quantify the model's ability to filter these categories across datasets like AUDIOCAPS and CLOTHO.
